                             O R D E R
Heard Mr. Vipin Sanghi, learned Senior Counsel for the
petitioner and Mr. Rajiv Shakdher, learned Senior Counsel
for the respondent.
2. Pursuant to the earlier orders, both the sides agree
that the matter being referred to the learned Mediator, is
progressing in the right direction, however, the pace is
slow. Some issues have been flagged by learned Senior
Counsel for the petitioner with regard to the behaviour of
the daughter, which is causing an impediment for the issue
to proceed in the manner, as desired. However, it has also
been stated that the sessions with the Counsellor are
helping and only when it comes to the time to be spent
with the petitioner-father, issue arises.
3. Learned Senior Counsel for the respondent submits that
besides the child, there are some ancillary issues, like
providing of a suitable accommodation/some amount of fixed
deposit in the name of the daughter.
4. However, both the learned Senior Counsel submit that
as the issue is likely to be sorted out before the learned
Mediator, the Court may not go into the same, for the
present.
5. Having considered the matter, we find that there
2

--- Page 346 ---
SLP(C) NO.3712/2025
appears to be some inhibition with the daughter whenever
she is in the company of the petitioner-father. Though,
parties  admit  that  there  has  been  progress  from  the
initial days, but still the same is not enough to indicate
that the daughter would be able to fully accept and adjust
in  the  company  of  the  petitioner-father  without  the
presence of the respondent-mother, or any other person.
6. Having considered the same, we request the learned
Mediator to go into the issue with regard to how best, at
present, the issue can be addressed during visitation or
even with regard to the daughter being allowed to go for
overnight  stay  or  even  a  short  vacation  with  the
petitioner- father. On these aspects, it shall be open to
the parties to put forward their views before the learned
Mediator, who will take a call on the same, keeping in
mind the interest of the child, so that it does not result
in any fresh trauma to her.
7. For the said purpose, as we are informed that there
may be some interim orders by some Courts below with
regard to visitation/travelling with regard to the child
with either of the parent alone, or if they agree for even
joint travel/short vacation, all such orders shall not
come  in  the  way  of  the  learned  Mediator  making  any
arrangement, which in his view would aid and facilitate
the daughter to fully accept both the parties as her
3

--- Page 347 ---
SLP(C) NO.3712/2025
parents, and which may help in getting over the trauma,
which she currently faces at times.
8. The matter be listed on 26.11.2026 at 2.00 p.m.
9. In the meantime, we request the learned Mediator to
keep us updated with regard to the status of the exercise
undertaken. The Counsellor shall also submit her report to
the learned Mediator, who in turn shall forward the same
to this Court.

set aside, and the case is remanded to the High Court for

--- Page 380 ---
2
                             O R D E R
1.  Learned counsel appearing on behalf of the respondent-Indian
Oil Corporation Limited (IOCL) prays for time to seek instruction
in respect of settlement. She has further stated that she has been
given instruction that the parties are ready for settlement.
2. On the other hand, learned senior counsel appearing for the
petitioners has stated before this Court that during the pendency
of the appeal before the High Court at Calcutta in the year 2023,
the rent of the property was fixed by way of an interim order.
Specifically, on 28.08.2023, the ad-hoc occupational charges were
fixed at Rs.1 Lakh per month. He has further stated that in the
same vicinity, the property value has gone high, and the similar
property fetches more than Rs.4 lakh per month. Therefore, till the
matter is settled between the parties, the respondent-IOCL should
be directed to pay rent/occupational charges to the petitioner as
per the prevailing market rate. 
3.  This Court is of considered opinion that the respondent-IOCL
is occupying the property in question, the IOCL is certainly
required to pay occupational charges. Let occupational charges be
paid to the petitioner at the rate of Rs.2 Lakh per month with
effect from 12.03.2026 (date of impugned judgment and order passed
by the High Court of Calcutta in APD No.11 of 2023 with CS No.83 of
2019). Let the arrears be paid within one week and IOCL will
continue to pay occupational charges till the matter is decided by
this Court or a compromise takes place.

IN THE SUPREME COURT OF INDIA
CIVIL APPELLATE JURISDICTION
CIVIL APPEAL  NO.         OF 2026
(@ SLP(C) No.26473/2023)
K                                              APPELLANT(S)
                                VERSUS
GOVT. OF NCT OF DELHI & ORS.                  RESPONDENT(S)
                       
O R D E R
         
1. Leave granted.
2. The appellant is aggrieved by the orders of the High
Court dated 23.01.2019 and 13.09.2023, passed in the
writ  petition  and  the  letters  patent  appeal,
respectively. By the said orders, the appointment of
Respondent No. 4 as Special Public Prosecutor to
represent the appellant in the Sessions Case No.
1006/2009  under  the  Scheduled  Castes  and  the
Scheduled  Tribes  (Prevention  of  Atrocities)  Act,
1989, is set aside.
3. We have heard the learned Senior Counsel appearing
for the petitioner, the learned Additional Solicitor
General, and the learned counsel appearing for the
respondents.
4. We have also perused the impugned judgment dated
13.09.2023 passed in LPA No. 252/2019. 
5. In our considered view, the High Court has adopted a

--- Page 386 ---
2
hyper - technical approach in passing the impugned
order. The very object of Rule 4(5) of the Scheduled
Castes  and  the  Scheduled  Tribes  (Prevention  of
Atrocities) Rules, 1995 is to facilitate the victim
to get assistance. The same has been given by the
state.  Merely  because  an  assistance  has  been
provided, as sought for by the appellant with respect
to the appointment of Respondent No. 4 as Special
Public Prosecutor, the trial would not be vitiated,
and in any case the accused will not be prejudiced.
6. In view of the same, we have no hesitation in setting
aside  the  impugned  order  in  LPA  No.  252/2019
confirming the order passed in W.P. (C) No.729/2018,
and  restoring  the  order  of  the  appointment  of
Respondent No. 4 made by the State.
7. The appeal is allowed, accordingly.
8. Pending application(s), if any, shall stand disposed
of.

Leave granted. 
 We have heard the learned counsel appearing
for  the  appellants/applicants  and  the  learned
counsel appearing for the respondent. 
The  appellants/applicants  have  been
convicted  for  the  offences  punishable  under
Section 6 of the Prevention of Children from
Sexual Offences Act, 2012 (for short, “POCSO”) by
the Trial Court, and were sentenced to undergo
life imprisonment, along with fine and default
stipulations. The judgment of conviction and order
on sentence rendered by the Trial Court, has been
confirmed by the High Court,  vide the impugned
order.  Aggrieved  by  the  same,  the
appellants/applicants are before this Court. 
We are conscious that the facts of the case
are disturbing to say the less. However, on the
earlier  occasion,  this  Court  vide  order  dated
14.02.2026, while declining the application for
suspension of sentence stated that the same can be
filed after completion of sentence of 10 years.
Now, admittedly, the appellants/applicants
2

--- Page 399 ---
have completed sentence of 10 years. The Criminal
Appeals are stated to be taken up for hearing.
In such view of the matter, we are inclined
to  grant  suspension  of  sentence  only  on  the
premise  that  the  appellants/applicants  have
already undergone substantial period of sentence
of 10 years.
Accordingly, the sentence imposed upon the
appellants/applicants  stands  suspended.  The
applicants/appellants are granted bail during the
pendency of the present appeals, subject to the
terms and conditions that may be imposed by the
concerned Trial Court.
IA  No.  158315/2026  in   SLP(Crl.)  No.
9624/2026  and  prayer  for  interim  relief  in
SLP(Crl.) No.11822/2026 are allowed, accordingly.

Petition for Special Leave to Appeal (C)  No.33196/2026
[Arising  out  of  impugned  final  judgment  and  order  dated

Punjab & Haryana at Chandigarh]
UNION OF INDIA & ORS.                              Petitioner(s)
                                VERSUS
BHARAT INDUSTRIAL ENTERPRISES PVT LTD              Respondent(s)
(IA No. 283537/2026 - EXEMPTION FROM FILING C/C OF THE IMPUGNED
JUDGMENT)
 
Date : 18-09-2026 This matter was called on for hearing today.
CORAM : 
         HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE J.B. PARDIWALA
         HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE K. VINOD CHANDRAN
For Petitioner(s) : Mr. N. Venkataraman, ASG
Mr. Sudarshan Lamba, AOR
Mr. V.C. Bharathi, Adv.
Mr. Bhuvan Kapoor Adv.
Mr. Harsh Nithin Gokhle, Adv.  
                 
#For Respondent(s) : 
          UPON hearing the counsel the Court made the following
                             O R D E R
1. Heard Mr. N. Venkatarman, the learned ASG appearing for the
1

--- Page 419 ---
SLP(C)  No.33196/2026
Revenue.
2. By the impugned Judgment, the High Court has declared Section
147A of the Income Tax Act 1961, (for short, “the Act, 1961”),
as unconstitutional.
3. Broadly, three questions arise for our consideration:-
(i) Whether the High Court erred in holding that the
notices under Section 148 and Section 148A respectively
must be issued only by the Faceless Assessing Officer more
particularly when Section 144B, the sole repository of the
Faceless Regime, makes no reference to Sections 148 and
148A respectively and the scheme dated 29.03.2022 framed
under  Section  151A  restricts  the  application  of  the
faceless manner to the extent provided in Section 144B? 
(ii) Whether the High Court erred in holding that the
notices under Section 148 and 148A respectively must be
issued only by the Faceless Assessing Officer, overlooking
the fact that no Notification under Section 120 was ever
issued by the Board which empowered the Faceless Assessing
Officer  to  perform  such  functions  or  ousted  the
jurisdiction of the Jurisdictional Assessing Officer from
performing such functions? 
(iii) Whether the High Court erred in holding that Section
147A does not pass the muster of a Validation Enactment,
overlooking  the  fact  that  Section  147A  operates
notwithstanding any Judgement, Section 151A and the Scheme
dated 29.03.2022 framed under Section 151A, and prescribes
the Assessing Officer for the purposes of Sections 148 and
148A respectively, which is not the Faceless Assessing
2

--- Page 420 ---
SLP(C)  No.33196/2026
Officer,  thereby  removing  the  defect  pointed  out  by
various High Courts and clarifying the position as to who
the Assessing Officer is?
4. Leave granted.
5. The impugned judgment and order passed by the High Court
shall remain stayed from its operation on the condition that the
assessment  and  reassessment  proceedings  shall  not  proceed
further till the final disposal of the main matter.
6. Notify this appeal for final hearing on 03.12.2026.
(CHANDRESH)                                     (POOJA SHARMA)
ASTT. REGISTRAR-cum-PS                        COURT MASTER (NSH)
#appearance not given.

          UPON hearing the counsel the Court made the following
                             O R D E R
1. The petitioners have been denied anticipatory bail by two
Courts in connection with FIR being No.  156/2026 dated 28.04.2026
registered with Police Station Sabalgarh, Morena District , for the
offence punishable under Sections 316(5) and 3(5) of the Bharatiya
Nyaya Sanhitha, 2023 respectively.

--- Page 484 ---
2
2. The petitioners, who were public servants, are accused of
wrongfully retaining an official government record. The petitioners
were denied anticipatory bail by the High Court on the ground that
the missing official records are uncovered till date and that the
petitioners were in custody of the said records at the relevant
time.
3. Notice was issued by this Court on 21.07.2026,  wherein, a
direction was passed not to take any coercive steps against the
petitioners, subject to their cooperation with the investigation.
4. In the facts and circumstances of this case and considering
submissions of the petitioners’ counsel, we are of the opinion that
the material against the petitioners falls short of the threshold
required for refusal of anticipatory bail. 
5. The Learned Counsel for the State has also submitted that the
petitioners are cooperating with the investigation.
6. Therefore, we order that in the event of arrest of the
petitioners in connection with the offence enumerated above, they
shall be released on bail, subject to terms and conditions that the
Investigating Officer (for short “I.O.”) may deem fit to impose. 
7. Once the petitioners are released on bail by the I.O., on
directions  issued  by  the  I.O.  or  summons  issued  by  the
jurisdictional court, the petitioners shall appear before the
jurisdictional court and furnish fresh bail bonds and ensure due
appearance in the trial.
8. With the aforesaid, these petitions stand disposed of.
9. Pending application(s), if any, also stand disposed of.

Petition for Special Leave to Appeal (Crl.)  No.17492/2026
[Arising out of impugned final judgment and order dated  23-07-2026
in IA No. 9003/2026 passed by the High Court of Madhya Pradesh at
Indore]
BALU @ BALRAM & ORS.                               Petitioner(s)
                                VERSUS
THE STATE OF MADHYA PRADESH                        Respondent(s)
(FOR ADMISSION)
(IA  No.  268381/2026  -  EXEMPTION  FROM  FILING  O.T.,  IA
No. 268383/2026 - EXEMPTION FROM SURRENDERING WITHIN TIME AND IA
No.  268379/2026  -  PERMISSION  TO  FILE  ADDITIONAL  DOCUMENTS/
FACTS/ANNEXURES)
 
Date : 18-09-2026 This matter was called on for hearing today.
CORAM : 
         HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE J.B. PARDIWALA
         HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE K. VINOD CHANDRAN
For Petitioner(s) : Mr. Pranjal Kishore , AOR
Mr. Nagarjun Sahu, Adv.
Ameerunnisa, Adv.
For Respondent(s) : 
Mr. Surjeet Singh, Adv.
Mr. Raghvendra Shukla, Adv.
Mr. P.N. Razdan, AOR
          UPON hearing the counsel the Court made the following
                             O R D E R 
1. This matter has come up today to consider the plea of the
petitioners (convicts) for suspension of sentence of rigorous
imprisonment for 3 years and release on bail, pending the
final disposal of their criminal appeal before the High Court,
which is already admitted.
2. It is alleged that on 24.04.2025, the petitioners with the
intention to murder the complainant assaulted him with bricks
and sticks, causing injury. 

--- Page 490 ---
2
3. We take notice of the fact that the petitioners were put to
trial for the offence punishable under Sections 109 r/w 3(5),
296 and 351(3) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhitha, 2023 (for
short “BNS”).
4. The Trial Court, relying on the eyewitness testimony, held the
petitioners guilty of the alleged crime and sentenced them to
undergo rigorous imprisonment for 3 years and to pay fine of
Rs.1,000/- (Rupees One Thousand only), each, and in default,
to undergo imprisonment for six months, in S.T.No.18/2025
arising out of FIR No.81/2025 registered in Police Station
Jharda, Ujjain District.
5. Being dissatisfied with the dismissal of their suspension of
sentence application by the High Court, the petitioners filed
this Special Leave Petition before us.
6. We take note of the fact that petitioner no. 1 has been in
jail for 114 days, while petitioners nos. 2 and 3 underwent
incarceration for 72 days and 104 days, respectively.
 
7. On a prima facie consideration, we are of the opinion that the
sentence  imposed  on  the  petitioners  can  be  suspended
considering the non-recording of injury as grievous.
8. In view of the aforesaid, we suspend the substantive order of
sentence of rigorous imprisonment for 3 years and fine imposed
on the petitioners and order that the petitioners be released
on bail forthwith, if not required in any other case, subject
to terms and conditions that the Additional Sessions Judge,
Mahidpur, may deem fit to impose, pending the final disposal
of their appeal before the High Court.
9. With the above directions, the Special Leave Petition is
disposed of.
10. Pending application(s), if any, shall also stand disposed of.
 (VISHAL ANAND)                                    (POOJA SHARMA)
DEPUTY REGISTRAR                                 COURT MASTER (NSH)

bringing  an  IAS  Officer  on  deputation  with  the

                   Mr. Kumar Mangalam, Adv.

                   Mr. Shrey Ravi Dambhare, AOR
Mr. Aditya Vaibhav Singh, G.A. 
Mr. Hanmat Lodhi, Adv. 
                   
          UPON hearing the counsel the Court made the following
                             O R D E R
1. This Special Leave Petition arises from an order
dated 23.02.2026 passed by the High Court of Madhya
Pradesh at Jabalpur rejecting the anticipatory bail
prayer  of  the  petitioner  in  connection  with
complaint case RCT No. 673/2025.
1

--- Page 588 ---
2. On  18.03.2026,  we  had  passed  an  interim
protection  order.  However,  today  we  have  been
apprised of the fact that there is a decision of
this Court rendered in  Om  Prakash  Chhawnika  vs.
State  of  Jharkhand  &  Anr. 1,  wherein it has been
observed that in connection with a complaint case
where court take cognizance and issue summons and no
non-bailable  warrants  are  issued,  there  is  no
apprehension  of  arrest  and,  therefore,  an
anticipatory bail prayer need not be entertained,
what the accused can do is to join the proceedings.
3. In such view of the matter, as it is not pointed
out that any non-bailable warrants have been issued,
we deem it appropriate to dispose of this petition
by giving liberty to the petitioner to join the
proceedings and take appropriate steps in light of
the order of this Court in  Om  Prakash  Chhawnika
(supra).
4. Accordingly, the Special Leave Petition stands
disposed of.
5. Interim protection order passed earlier stands
discharged.
6. Pending  application(s),  if  any,  shall  stand
disposed of.        
(CHETAN ARORA)                                  (SAPNA BANSAL)

1

--- Page 750 ---
passed,  transferring  the  petitioner  to  Madhya  Pradesh

petitioner apprehends that he may not get salary in Madhya
Pradesh, because another person is already working on that
post. Once a person is transferred by entertaining the
representation and a formal order to this effect has
already been issued, non-payment of salary would not arise.
3. The Special Leave Petition is dismissed subject to
the above observation.

of.
